- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast decline, check for mean reversion — if sentiment remains bullish, allow slight lagged correction.  
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 20–40% in 3–5 day window.  
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to overcorrect; dampen forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often overestimates; apply 1–3% downward bias unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative signals (e.g., -1.00 repeated), model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.
